Problem: Find the sum of the digits of \(11 \cdot 101 \cdot 111 \cdot 110011\).

<reflection>
The problem asks for the digit sum of \(11 \cdot 101 \cdot 111 \cdot 110011\). \(11 \cdot 101 = 1111\). \(1111 \cdot 111 = 123321\). \(123321 \cdot 110011 = 123321 \cdot 110000 + 123321 \cdot 11\). \(123321 \cdot 110000 = 13565310000\).
The addition is incorrect: \(1233210 + 123321 = 1356531\), not \(1245541\).
Recompute \(123321 \cdot 11\) correctly, then add it to \(13565310000\) and sum the digits of the corrected product.
</reflection>
